- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) or shows strong downward momentum, model often underestimates drop; increase forecast low end by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.7), model shows mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 5–7 day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the window; apply a 1–3% downward bias to first 5–7 forecast points.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “negative” signals, model underperforms; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast tail (last 5–7 days).
